title: Temporal dynamics of early life stages of fish in a mangrove tidal creek
content:
Abstract
Estuarine mangrove forests are recognized as important nursery grounds for many fish species. However, data on larval and juvenile fish communities within neotropical tidal creeks remain limited, especially compared to the extensive research on ichthyoplankton in deeper, navigable estuarine channels. To address this gap, monthly day and night samples were collected using a modified channel net (500 μm) in a secondary mangrove creek in the Itamaracá Estuarine System, northeastern Brazil. Water temperature, salinity and oxygen saturation were measured at the sampling site. A total of 19 673 early life stage fish (including 11 457 larvae) were collected, representing 27 families, with Atherinopsidae, Dorosomatidae, Gerreidae, Gobiidae and Engraulidae being the most abundant. Although overall fish abundance and diversity did not show significant diel or seasonal differences, some families exhibited distinct responses to environmental conditions, such as Atherinopsidae occurring consistently throughout the year and Dorosomatidae and Gerreidae showing increased abundance under conditions of higher oxygen saturation. The dominance of postflexion larvae (65% of the total) indicates the critical role of mangrove tidal creeks in supporting this early developmental stage of fishes, thereby providing niches for feeding and shelter. This study highlights the importance of tidal creeks as pivotal habitats for fish populations, contributing to the conservation of estuarine biodiversity.
